correctness.rationale: Definition and exact polygon vertices follow Ostrovski 2013 Theorem 5.1 and Lemma 5.2. The determinant of the corner matrix is 1; the algebraic identity det(v,Bv)=-t(1-2s) was checked symbolically modulo s^2=t-t^2. Fourfold-centered shoelace gives A=1-2t-2Kt(1-2s). Polarizing the preserved indefinite form yields cosh(K mu)=1/(2t); positive branch arcosh expansions give K=1/epsilon+1/3+O(epsilon), hence A=10/(3K^2)+O(K^-3). Bundled verifier independently computes polygon areas for K=3,4,8,12, checks exact algebra, and approaches the constant numerically; finite tests are supporting only.

originality.rationale: The 2013 primary manuscript was read in its publicly accessible HTML version, including its map definition (Sections 2-3), polygonal return construction and complete annulus foliation (Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.4), Appendix return parameter formula, and the discussion. It proves the existence of the annulus but neither its exact area nor the quadratic exhaustion rate. The new signed-area telescope plus an independent quadratic-form hyperbolic-time calculation produces the coefficient 10/3. Targeted the published-finding index semantic queries for Ostrovski, exceptional integrable annulus area, and K^-2 shrinkage returned geometrically different findings without implication. The result is a quantitative consequence of the original construction and is therefore not offered as a new invariant-circle existence theorem. Full priority beyond inspected sources cannot be guaranteed.
residual_risks: Ostrovski 2013 explicitly constructs the polygon; a reader may obtain the new area quantity by additional geometry, so publication priority requires separate human expert review.
A later paper or unpublished note could have evaluated the area; searched literature cannot establish exhaustive priority.
The full text of the analogous discretized-rotation work was not inspected; its different phase space reduces but does not eliminate bibliographic uncertainty.

value.rationale: The area of the complement of a proven integrable invariant-circle foliation is a natural measure-theoretic invariant for the 2013 exceptional parameter sequence. The theorem strengthens the previously qualitative phrase large parts to an exact area formula and a sharp measure-exhaustion rate, revealing cancellation of the naively leading O(1/K) contributions and a meaningful O(1/K^2) residual. It quantifies how much of the phase square is certified integrable without unsupported assertions about its core.
